espn-603999.headline: South Africa need a win in Paris just to stay first
beats: South Africa have been first in the world since 31 August and have won nine of their last 10 Tests against France. Anything short of a win at the Stade de France hands first place to New Zealand.
France lost the last meeting at home, 17–32, on 8 November 2025. Last weekend France put eight tries past Fiji, and South Africa put nine past Italy.

The scrum-halves are 65-cap Antoine Dupont and 12-cap Morne van den Berg, whose first start of 2026 came only in the September decider against New Zealand. Schalk Burger has warned that France are "unstoppable" with Dupont back.
New Zealand are already level with South Africa on table points in their conference. They would happily take the ranking as well.

espn-604000.headline: Argentina are short of hookers. Italy are short of wins.
beats: Julián Montoya failed an HIA in Dublin, and Leonel Oviedo was tested repeatedly in a game that ended with uncontested scrums. Both are doubts for Genova and Ignacio Ruiz is out, so Felipe Contepomi has called up Facundo Bosch, whose last cap came in 2021, and Bautista Bernasconi.

The back three is no healthier. Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee against Ireland, and Santiago Carreras and Benjamín Elizalde are injured. The fullback may be a new name, or Gerónimo Prisciantelli, the back-up fly-half.
Italy have lost five straight. Last week a depleted side let in nine tries to South Africa, all converted, and lost 7–66. A win here would lift them to 9th, above Wales and Fiji.
Argentina go to France next. Italy host Fiji, the other side still on nil points, which is a fixture they would rather not need.

espn-604001.headline: New Zealand can rotate. Wales cannot afford to
beats: Last November New Zealand scored 52 in Cardiff. Since then they have put 43 or more on Australia twice and Scotland once, seven tries each time. Now they talk of rotation, with Will Jordan out with a hamstring tear: "We can make quite a few changes, still put a damn good side in."

Wales have less room. Aaron Wainwright, 71 caps, is their most experienced forward and most effective forward ball-carrier, and he did not train on Tuesday. Taine Basham is next in line, and has not played for Wales since the 2024 Six Nations.
Wales beat Japan 28–21 on 7 November. In July, South Africa held them scoreless. A win here takes them above Fiji into ninth in the world, which is still a long way from second.
Louis Rees-Zammit has spoken about ending the winless streak against them. New Zealand have spoken about who gets an opportunity.

espn-604002.headline: Beating Australia by 23 cost England four players
beats: Feyi-Waboso's ankle has ended his autumn. Furbank, Chessum and Atkinson are rehabbing in camp with New Zealand in mind. That leaves Steve Borthwick three new starters in the backline and one at blindside.
Henry Pollock scored twice on the wing off the bench against Australia, and is unlikely to start there. With Tom Curry out for November and no Pepper or Underhill, the back row may need him more.

Japan lost 21–28 to Wales in Cardiff, near enough for a bonus point, and are the Pacific Nations Cup champions. A Japan win drops England to seventh, below Scotland and the Australia side they just put 45 past.
England have never lost to Japan in six meetings, the last 59–14. The selection is about New Zealand. The result still has to be about Japan.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland keep winning and keep losing number eights
beats: Sean Jansen's home debut ended early in the second half of the 42–12 win over Argentina, and his knee keeps him out for the rest of the campaign. Caelan Doris and Jack Conan were already injured. Uncapped Ulster forward David McCann has been called up to fill the gap.

The captaincy has gone the same way. Dan Sheehan led the squad in Doris's absence, took a concussion against Argentina, and misses Fiji under a 12-day return-to-play protocol. He is a doubt for the following game as well.
Fiji conceded 54 away to France last weekend and have no points from four games. Mack Hansen still warns of a stiff test, and a Fiji win would drop Ireland to 5th, below France and England.
South Africa follow at the same ground on 21 November. By then Ireland would like a few forwards back.

espn-604004.headline: Both lost 21–43 to New Zealand. One gets over it
beats: Australia lost 21–43 to New Zealand at home on 17 October. Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at home on 7 November. Same score, a month apart, and neither side has won since.

Australia then went to Twickenham and lost 22–45, their third straight defeat. Captain Harry Wilson's verdict was that "we weren't physical enough to slow their ball down". They come to Murrayfield without one of their breakout stars for the rest of the Championship.
Scotland have recalled Ali Price at scrum-half in place of Gus Warr, who has gone back to Sale. Lose, and they hand sixth in the world to Australia.
Scotland have won 13 of the 35 meetings, and none of the 16 between 1982 and 2009. The loser takes that 43 into the following Saturday: Scotland at home to Japan, Australia away to Wales.

espn-604005.headline: The autumn England beat New Zealand ended a coach's tenure
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. That autumn ended in a player review that cost Scott Robertson his job, and Dave Rennie has the side now.

Steve Hansen calls Rennie's side a "different team", built largely from the same players. They have scored 50, 43 and 43 in their last three, and kept Scotland scoreless after half-time at Murrayfield.

England have won three straight. The last was 45–22 over Australia, and it cost them Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the rest of the autumn. One of the six call-ups is Max Hicks, born in Auckland and a Māori All Black in 2022, who could make his Test debut against New Zealand.
Win by 16 or more and England go up to third in the world. New Zealand are level on points with South Africa at the top of the table, and know better than most what losing to England can cost.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland keep scoring tries and keep letting in 43
beats: Scotland scored three tries against New Zealand at Murrayfield and still lost 21–43, the same score Ireland put on them in March. Even the win in Argentina in July finished 47–38.

Japan can score: 63 against the USA and 57 against Canada in September. They have lost their last two, though, and the 21–28 defeat in Cardiff earned them only a bonus point. The BBC's verdict was that Wales were the side with a lot to prove.
Japan have slid from 9th to 12th in the world since October. A win by 16 or more at Murrayfield would put them straight back to 9th and drop Scotland to 8th.
Jack Dempsey says a move to Japan will keep him fresh and hungry for next year's World Cup. Scotland's first job is keeping Japan out.

espn-604007.headline: Ireland's scrum meets the side that took it apart
beats: In their last meeting, at the Aviva in November 2025, South Africa won 24–13. They took six scrum penalties off Ireland, plus a penalty try. Andrew Porter and Paddy McCarthy were both shown yellow cards for scrum offences, and Porter did not play for Ireland again until this month.

Against Argentina the Irish scrum won two penalties, one of them Porter's, and conceded none. Scrum coach John Fogarty thinks it is heading the right way. South Africa have just put 66 points on Italy, and Rassie Erasmus still says they "have to play much better against France and Ireland".

The hooker is the worry. Dan Sheehan, captain while Caelan Doris is injured, was concussed against Argentina and is going through a 12-day return-to-play protocol. Sean Jansen's knee has already ended his tournament.
An Irish win would drop South Africa below New Zealand in the world rankings. The front row would settle for getting the scrum penalties back.

espn-604008.headline: Italy's first win of the series is worth two places
beats: Italy are bottom of the 12-team table on nought from four, with a points difference of minus 153. Fiji are one place above them on the same nought, at minus 133.

Neither defence has held. Italy conceded 66 at home to South Africa and 57 in Australia. Fiji let in 54 in France, though they did beat Japan 34–28 in October, which is more than Italy managed against Japan in July.
Win in Udine and Italy climb from 11th in the world to 9th, above Fiji and Wales: two places for beating the only other side in the series without a point.
First, Italy host Argentina in Genoa, and Fiji meet an Ireland without their captain, Dan Sheehan. If both stay last in their conferences, the 11th-place final puts them straight back together.

espn-604009.headline: Argentina's year ends against France's 42-point habit
beats: France have scored at least 42 in each of their last three Tests, the latest eight tries in a 54–17 win over Fiji. Argentina conceded 42 on their last outing, away to Ireland, and scored two tries.

Argentina's single win this year flatters nobody, but their home results were tighter. They lost to South Africa by seven, lost to Australia by six, then drew 28–28 with Australia. Away to Ireland the margin was 30, and this one is away too.

Schalk Burger calls France "unstoppable" with Antoine Dupont back. France start the day top of the North, two points clear of England, and a defeat would also put them below England in the world rankings.
After this, Argentina's next game is Canada at the World Cup in October 2027. That is a long time to sit with whatever Saint-Denis gives them.

espn-604010.headline: Australia have let in 40-plus three times running
beats: New Zealand put 50 and 43 on Australia in October, and England added 45 in London on 8 November. Their last win was 42–38 over South Africa in September, which shows they can score. It says less about who tackles.
The England defeat also brought rugby's first yellow card for a hip drop tackle, shown to Bell. Steve Hansen singled out a Wallabies failing he said took no talent to fix.

Wales offer no fortress. They lost 0–43 in South Africa in July, then beat Japan 28–21 with four tries. New Zealand come to Cardiff first, possibly without Aaron Wainwright, who hurt a leg against Japan.

Win here and Wales go up to ninth in the world, with Australia down to eighth, below Argentina, the side they could only draw with in September. After this, Australia's next game is Hong Kong at the World Cup in October 2027. That is a long time to think about tackling.
